in_english.name: Blayne
in_english.long_meaning: The name Blayne is thought to be derived from the surname Blain, possibly from the Gaelic word blàs, meaning 'flourishing' or 'wholesome'. It is also related to the name Blaine, which is an anglicized form of the Gaelic name Blàthain, meaning 'fair-haired' or 'white-haired'. Historically, the name Blayne has been associated with the Christian tradition, as a variant of the name Blain, which is found in the Bible as a place-name.

data.cultural_impact: Although not commonly used in modern English-speaking countries, Blayne was a popular boys' name in the Middle Ages, particularly in Wales and England. It was also the name of several medieval saints, including Saint Blaise, the patron saint of throats and animals, and Saint Blayne the Martyr.
